newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK SAYS CORPORATE CREDIT GROWTH NOW KEY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK SAYS CORPORATE CREDIT GROWTH NOW KEY.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland is now more concerned with growth in corporate credit than with consumer credit expansion which slowed after buoyant 1996, NBP deputy head told Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki newspaper.

"Consumer credit is not a problem, it has grown very fast in 1996 but now its growth has slowed down. Now there is a question of corporate credit which accounts for most of the credit volume and generates money supply," Kozinski said.
Kozinski said the growth of lending to commercial entities slowed-down in the September 1996-March 1997 period but still remained a concern.
"The actual level of corporate credit remains high and is not falling," he said.
Kozinski said the central bank would strive to control credit creation at commercial banks but declined to say how the central bank intended to control the corporate credit expansion
